questions.stem: Which statement best describes data ownership?
options: A broad framework ensuring data quality, availability, usability and security across an organisation
The concept that defines the rights and responsibilities associated with data, specifying who has control over it
The technical process of backing up databases
The cross-functional assignment of stewardship roles
A set of standards for how data is stored in the cloud
questions.explanation: Data ownership defines the rights and responsibilities attached to data, including who has authority over its collection, storage, access and usage. It focuses on the 'who' of data control.

questions.stem: Data ownership is described as focusing on which aspect of data control?
options: The 'how' aspect: the processes used to manage data
The 'when' aspect: retention periods for data
The 'who' aspect: determining who has the ultimate say over the data
The 'where' aspect: physical storage location
The 'why' aspect: business justification for collecting data
questions.explanation: Data ownership is more focused on the 'who' aspect of data control, determining who holds decision-making authority over the data.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a responsibility of a data owner?
options: Being accountable for ensuring data is handled in compliance with laws, regulations and internal policies
Writing the organisation-wide data governance framework
Assigning stewardship roles across every department
Defining the enterprise data lifecycle for all datasets
Compressing data to reduce storage costs
questions.explanation: The data owner is accountable for ensuring the data they control is handled in compliance with relevant laws, regulations and internal policies.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes data governance?
options: The right of one individual to decide who may access a dataset
A method of encrypting data at rest
A broader framework and set of practices ensuring high data quality, availability, usability and security across the organisation
The archiving of historical records for legal reasons
The role of a single business unit that controls a dataset
questions.explanation: Data governance is the broader framework of policies, procedures and roles that manage and control data throughout its lifecycle to ensure quality, availability, usability and security.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as something data governance encompasses?
options: Data quality
Data stewardship
Data management
Compliance
Individual authority to override all organisational policies
questions.explanation: Data governance encompasses data quality, data stewardship, data management and compliance. Nothing in it grants an individual authority to override organisational policies.

questions.stem: In terms of scope, how do data ownership and data governance differ?
options: Data ownership addresses the organisation-wide framework; data governance addresses individual accountability
Data ownership focuses on individual accountability and decision-making authority; data governance addresses the broader framework and processes across the organisation
Both have identical scope and are interchangeable terms
Data ownership covers only technical systems; data governance covers only legal matters
Data governance is limited to a single dataset; data ownership spans all datasets
questions.explanation: Ownership is scoped to individual accountability and decision authority, while governance addresses the broader, organisation-wide framework and processes for managing data.

questions.stem: How do data ownership and data governance differ in terms of responsibilities?
options: Ownership deals with specific individuals or units responsible for particular datasets; governance takes a cross-functional approach assigning responsibilities to various roles
Ownership is cross-functional; governance is limited to one person
Both assign responsibility exclusively to the IT department
Neither assigns any responsibilities
Ownership assigns responsibility to external regulators; governance to internal staff
questions.explanation: Data ownership assigns specific individuals or units to particular datasets, whereas data governance involves a cross-functional approach with responsibilities spread across various organisational roles.

questions.stem: What is the focus of data governance compared with data ownership?
options: Governance emphasises control and decision rights; ownership emphasises quality
Governance emphasises storage cost; ownership emphasises speed
Both emphasise decision rights only
Governance emphasises overall management, quality and compliance of data; ownership emphasises control and decision rights over data
Governance emphasises hardware; ownership emphasises software
questions.explanation: Data ownership emphasises control and decision rights over data, while data governance emphasises the overall management, quality and compliance of data.

questions.stem: What is the relationship between data ownership and data governance?
options: They are unrelated concepts from different disciplines
Data governance is a component of data ownership
Data ownership is a component of data governance, which is the more comprehensive approach
Data ownership replaces data governance in modern organisations
They are exact synonyms
questions.explanation: Data ownership is a component of data governance; governance extends beyond individual ownership to organisation-wide policies and practices for responsible data management.

questions.stem: The head of a sales department is designated as the person with authority to decide how the customer contact dataset is collected, stored, accessed and used. Which concept does this illustrate?
options: Data governance
Data ownership
Data archiving
Data compression
Data integration
questions.explanation: Assigning decision authority over a specific dataset to an individual or organisational unit is data ownership, which is tied to individuals or units within a company.
